snippets.text: Imaging findings in sympathetic ophthalmia substantially overlap with VKH; therefore, imaging supports activity assessment and follow-up, but the history of ocular trauma or intraocular surgery remains decisive for diagnosis. In the acute phase, imaging may show multifocal choroiditis, optic disc swelling, serous retinal detachments, and, less commonly, MEWDS-like changes or retinal vasculitis with chorioretinitis. In the chronic phase, more informative findings include widespread mid- and far-peripheral chorioretinal atrophy, peripapillary subretinal fibrosis, and nummular perivascular atrophy. No single imaging sign is pathognomonic, but multimodal correlation is valuable both for supporting the diagnosis in the appropriate clinical context and for documenting persistent inflammatory activity or chronic structural damage over time. Compared with VKH, sympathetic ophthalmia shows substantial overlap on multimodal imaging, including bilateral stromal choroiditis, serous retinal detachment, choroidal thickening, optic disc leakage, and ICGA choroidal lesions. Bikbov et al. showed that a higher prevalence of myopic pathology blindness was associated with male gender (p < 0.001; OR = 2.32; 95% CI 1.47–3.66). However, one study reported that the incidence of myopia in females was higher than males. Li et al. found that girls had a higher prevalence than boys of hyperopia in grade 1 (P = 0.596) but a higher prevalence than myopic boys in grade 6 (P < 0.001).

snippets.text: To the best of our knowledge, this systematic review has evaluated associated risk factors for juvenile myopic patients. The results can be of great significance in future investigations. The novel protective metrics evaluation for preventing axial elongation and myopia development and various aspects of investigation contributed to early-onset myopia are two considerable strengths of this study. Limitations can be listed as follows: First, as it was a systematic review, selection bias might be common. Second, a relatively small number of RCTs associated with myopic risk factors analysis were included. Third, exploring possible reasons for myopic maculopathy and retinal alterations was significant in the future.

snippets.text: Since myopic eyes are large, large OCT scans (12 mm) are preferred. Scanning the entire posterior pole is imperative. OCT scans should be performed along the horizontal and vertical axis. Myopic traction maculopathy cannot be judged solely based on OCT. Fundus photographs are essential for the evaluation of the eye. Conventional 30-degree photographs do not help properly evaluate the staphyloma; therefore, wide-field fundus photos are preferred. They give the full extent and the location of the staphyloma.
